items.q: What are you usually addicted to after a breakup?
items.a: Not the person — **how you felt around them** (wanted, seen, chosen). You miss **who you thought you'd be with them**. Rebuild that state from self, friends, and community.

items.q: What is closure, if you never get the apology?
items.a: **Peace over answers.** Some chapters end without explanations. Healing is three steps forward and two back — a flood after weeks of strength is human, not failure.

items.q: Why is 'he plays guitar' the wrong relationship test?
items.a: He needs to be **great at a relationship**, not at music. Want guitar? Go to a John Mayer concert. Instagram-profile traits are not partner skill.

items.q: If they were amazing for eight weeks then ghosted, what do you have?
items.a: **Eight good weeks.** That action *is* the closure. If it should have and could have, **it would have** — the stolen-future script is science fiction.

items.q: What is the poet vs poetry distinction?
items.a: The **poet** is charm on a date. The **poetry** is the relationship someone will write for years, including rebuilding after a fight. Poets are common; poetry is rare.

items.q: How much energy should you give someone new?
items.a: A **casino chip** you don't mind losing. Five-minute rejection is cheaper than months of unequal energy. Play-it-cool attracts people who only want the unavailable.

sections.title: Barrett & Erivo: leftover contact and the lens

items.q: What is the desperate stage of a breakup?
items.a: Bargaining for **any leftover contact** while still in love (Barrett's *Motel*). It re-breaks you. Longest work: exit **codependency** and become the safe place for yourself.

items.q: How does the abandonment voice keep you stuck?
items.a: Its only goal is **don't be abandoned**. It people-pleases in the relationship, then rewrites history the night you leave. Erivo: expecting leave so it cannot hurt — and staying silent to keep people — is the same lens.

items.q: What kills most marriages, according to 25 years of divorce court?
items.a: **Disconnection** — from partner and from yourself — slowly then all at once. We go blind to what we see most. The dangerous lies are the ones we tell ourselves about what still makes us happy.

items.q: If willpower could make two people love each other, what would happen?
items.a: They would last. Sexton's kitchen-table line: **feeling-love is not enough** for this particular marriage. Love is **loaned, not gifted**. Happily ever after can mean separately.
